findings.finding: F1 — the route Dispatch actually resolves through, GET /v1/sessions (cmd/listener/api.go:681 sessionsHandler over sessions.List()), is cache-only and outside the spec's two fix sites, so a Dispatch mention or broadcast is still refused during a cache refill (internal/dispatch/api/envoy_resolve.go:97-102, comment_delivery.go:53, broadcasts.go:353-354).
findings.answer: Decision D10 in plan.md: out of scope and said so. A list cannot be made read-through per key; covering it means Dispatch resolving by session id, which is a different change and a seventh acceptance case. Reported to the architect as a candidate follow-up issue; this plan does not build it.

findings.finding: F2 — a one-minute retry bound cannot be delegated to the bus: finalize(true) NAKs at a fixed 30 s (delivery.go:75-84) and consumerMaxDeliver is 20 (durable.go:28-32), which is about 9.5 minutes, and nothing in packages/envoy consumes JetStream's max-deliveries advisory, so a message the server stops redelivering is dropped with no line and no counter.
findings.answer: Decision D2 and task T4: the bus redelivers, the listener owns the bound and the give-up record. NAK with a 5 s delay (deliveryMessage.finalizeAfter), give up when the message's JetStream age reaches the window or its delivery count reaches 18 (consumerMaxDeliver - 2), so the give-up line and counter always precede JetStream's silent stop. No change to the durable's policy.

findings.finding: F3 — retrying would publish one no_holder exception per attempt (delivery.go:577-586 publishes before the skip outcome), and the listener consumes its own exception subject (stream.go:88, durable.go:123), so each attempt would also write two more log lines.
findings.answer: Decision D6: the exception is published once, at give-up, and never during the retry window.

findings.finding: F4 — the branch the retry must reuse sets neither clearAttempt nor retry (delivery.go:581-586), and a redelivery whose attempt entry survives is swallowed as `listener attempt-dedupe skip` (delivery.go:530-539); the window must also fit inside the attempt cache's 5-minute TTL (main.go:707).
findings.answer: Task T4: both the retry and the give-up set clearAttempt, and a test asserts the two invariants window/delay + 2 <= consumerMaxDeliver and window < the attempt cache TTL.

findings.finding: F5 — the new read sits in front of a publish that already bounds itself at 5 s (bus/nats.go:793,835), which is exactly the caller's per-attempt deadline (envoy-client/src/transport.ts:6,249,263), so the server could spend 7 s and Dispatch's own client (internal/dispatch/envoy/client.go:85,107) records a miss as 'may already have landed'.
findings.answer: Decision D3 and tasks T1-T2: sendRequestBudget 3500 ms for the whole handler from r.Context(), sendSessionReadTimeout 1 s for the store read, the publish taking the remainder through the new bus.Client.PublishReportingDuplicateWithin/PublishWithin, which leave every other publisher on the existing 5 s. The role paths keep roleHolderReadTimeout at 2 s. Acceptance A3 asserts the answer arrives in under 4 s.

findings.finding: F6 — the six acceptance bullets have no state for 'the session bucket read did not answer', and today every error from the cache read becomes 404 (api.go:510-513), which is the confident-absence defect the issue is about.
findings.answer: Decision D4: it is answered 503 with the bus-unreachable body and Retry-After, following this listener's own rule (api.go:404-409) and the precedent at api.go:731-739, and it is read as inside the spec's bus-unreachable case rather than a seventh one. Reported to the architect as a reading it may overturn.

findings.finding: F7 — bullet 4 gives a permanently refused publish a retriable 503, which contradicts packages/envoy/AGENTS.md:1918 ('a publish the listener's grant does not allow is a 500 naming the server's violation') and tells every client to retry a failure that cannot succeed.
findings.answer: Decision D5: follow the spec. No client honours Retry-After today and envoy-client retries any status at or above 500 exactly once (transport.ts:281-284), so a permanent refusal is retried once, exactly as today's 500 already is. AGENTS.md:1918 is corrected in task T8.

findings.finding: F8 — the listener already answers 503 'service starting' on these very routes (main.go:449-462, asserted at main_test.go:78-82,193-197), and a caller or an alarm could not tell it from the new one.
findings.answer: Named in plan.md: one in-package constant busUnansweredPrefix = 'envoy: the message bus did not answer', distinct from 'service starting', carried by every new 503 so the tests and a deployed filter match one string.

findings.finding: F9 — several refusals have no destination to name and one class is refused before the body is trusted: a 401 is answered by the auth wrapper (apiauth.go:80) and the starting gate refuses before the mux (main.go:449-462).
findings.answer: Decision D9: the line is written in the two handlers, so it covers every request that reaches them; the 401 and the gate keep their own records, and task T8 says so in the documentation.

findings.finding: F10 — the line puts message text in the log for the two request kinds the spec names as outside the arrivals (an ad-hoc core publish and a request that fails before its publish lands), and internal/logging has no redaction.
findings.answer: Decision D8: the summary is logged on accepted and refused alike. It is the one-line payload summary the arrival line already carries for everything the stream captures (delivery.go:284), and a send that never reached the bus is the one message no other system holds.

findings.finding: F11 — the spec's volume figure is inferred because inbound requests are counted nowhere; a request counter would make it a count, but it is not in the acceptance.
findings.answer: Decision D11: not built. Bullet 6 asks for the line and for the give-up counter's label. Reported to the architect as declined scope.

findings.finding: F12 — this repository has three homes for a setting (internal/config/config.go's service-wide table, main.go's inline ENVOY_CI_DEBOUNCE, and unexported constants) and no table for listener settings, so the settable retry bound has no obvious home.
findings.answer: Decision D7: ENVOY_UNPLACEABLE_RETRY_WINDOW, read in cmd/listener/main.go exactly as ENVOY_CI_DEBOUNCE is (main.go:822-831), default 60 s, a value that does not parse logging one WARN naming the variable. It is listener-only, and the e2e rig already sets ENVOY_CI_DEBOUNCE (scripts/e2e-local.sh:144).

findings.finding: F13 — 'the lookup the deliverer uses' has two readings: inside session.Deliverer, which would add a context-taking method to SessionLookup (internal/session/lookup.go:3-7) and to every fake; or in the listener's delivery path, which already holds the concrete registry (delivery.go:48).
findings.answer: Decision D1 and task T3: the read goes in cmd/listener/delivery.go and the resolved entry is passed to HandleAgentMessage, which delivers through the existing DeliverWithResultForEntry (session.go:52-54). SessionLookup is unchanged, so no fake grows a method, and the bound has one definition.

findings.finding: F14 — the spec names two surfaces and assigns neither; e2e-local.sh asserts with curl -fsS, which exits non-zero on a refusal, and writes out/e2e/listener.log without asserting over it.
findings.answer: The acceptance table in plan.md gives every case a surface and an exact command, and task T7 extends e2e-local.sh with the curl -o/-w shape for the refusals and the first assertion over out/e2e/listener.log.

findings.finding: F15 — the behaviour this change replaces is written down in packages/envoy/AGENTS.md (lines about the send route, the grant violation, the attempt and dedupe caches), packages/envoy/docs/architecture.md (the route table and the exception table) and packages/envoy/CHANGELOG.md, and the delivery_status label set is documented nowhere.
findings.answer: Task T8 names each file and what changes in it, including the correction of AGENTS.md:1918 and a new home in docs/architecture.md for the status table, the request-line names and the delivery_status label set.

findings.finding: F16 — the durable is per machine over the whole subject list (bus/stream.go:51-53, durable.go:123,137), so every listener in the fleet consumes every agent message and would run the retry and the give-up record once each.
findings.answer: Recorded in plan.md's 'What the code does today': this is one give-up record per listener per message, exactly as one skip and one exception per listener is today, so it is no regression; stated so the tester reads two records on a two-listener rig as correct.
